findings.verdict: closed within the explicit ideal sheet model
findings.reason: Treat the specification as an exact planar electric-polarization sheet with transverse oscillator displacement, rather than claiming arbitrary discrete dipoles or a bulk effective medium imply it. Tangential E continuity gives e_t=e+e_r; the surface-current jump gives e_r=-P_dot/2. Therefore E_sheet=e-P_dot/2 and B_average=[(e-e_r)+e_t]/2=e. The causal oscillator has P_ddot+(f/2)*P_dot+P=f*e. For f>0 its homogeneous modes decay, so the retarded solution is unique. No added absorption channel is required.

The total longitudinal charge Lorentz force is P_dot*B_average=P_dot*e. The electric gradient evaluated symmetrically at the sheet is partial_x E_average=-e_dot, so the proposed source is -P*e_dot. Their difference is d(P*e)/dt. At leading order L_int=P*E+P*(V cross B)_y has canonical longitudinal momentum M1*V-P*B; its Euler-Lagrange equation gives kinetic force P*partial_x E+d(P*B)/dt. Thus the proposed source confuses canonical and kinetic frame acceleration, while its optical oscillator and both derivatives can be implemented exactly.

findings.verdict: correct at the stated leading order
findings.reason: At a zero-thickness sheet the exterior longitudinal momentum-flux difference is e^2+e_r^2-e_t^2=P_dot*e. The oscillator energy U=(P_dot^2+P^2)/(2*f) is positive, and U_dot=P_dot*(e-P_dot/2)=e^2-e_r^2-e_t^2. After the retarded excitation decays, integrating energy balance gives integral(P_dot*e)=integral(P_dot^2)/2=2*reflected_energy. This is the expected complete-pulse impulse. A finite-width reference must retain field momentum inside its control volume, or demonstrate its vanishing in the sheet limit; exterior stresses alone are not generally the finite-volume material force.

findings.verdict: correct order counting for a fixed finite clock
findings.reason: If the incident amplitude is a, fields and P are O(a), optical force and X,V are O(a^2)=O(E), and longitudinal spring/kinetic energy is O(a^4)=O(E^2). Motion-induced optical corrections therefore do not alter the leading O(E) force at a fixed clock. The transverse oscillator energy is already O(E) and is included. Its contribution to translating inertia times V is higher order. This supports extracting M*X2/E as E tends to zero before considering long-time behavior; it is not a full finite-amplitude moving-sheet simulation.

findings.verdict: well posed once clock and phase are fixed
findings.reason: For equal masses, Xcm_ddot=F/M and R_ddot+Omega_m^2*R=2*F/M. Since X2=Xcm-R/2, the stated kernel [t-s-sin(Omega_m*(t-s))/Omega_m] follows. Retarded zero mechanical initial conditions and a known positive Omega_m close the mechanics. Reflection leaves a nonzero shared drift, so a finite specified clock is essential. The readout retains translation and does not reduce to a deliberately zero rigid-limit signal.

findings.verdict: physical distinction exists, usable gap unproven
findings.reason: Integration by parts gives z-z_source=integral_{-infinity}^{t*}[1-cos(Omega_m*(t*-s))]*P(s)*e(s)/E ds, with vanishing retarded boundary terms. This need not vanish even though the complete-pulse impulses and stationary force averages agree. It can also be small or cancel. No numerical lower bound, stable ordinary-signal domain, noise margin or verifier runtime follows from the identity.

For harmonic incident amplitude e0 and I=abs(e0)^2/2, chi=f/[1-omega^2-i*f*omega/2] and R=f^2*omega^2/[4*(1-omega^2)^2+f^2*omega^2]. Averaged radiation force is 2*I*R for either force law because the average of d(Pe)/dt is zero. For positive f, nonzero off-resonant omega and nonzero I, R is strictly increasing. Exactly resonant omega makes R=1 and is unidentifying; large f or near-resonance settings can be poorly conditioned despite strict monotonicity. Fixed-noise robustness still requires checking.

KMXhb9w final coefficients use .5*Re(derivative@E.conj()) and .5*Im(derivative@E.conj()) instead of a real Poynting-vector term. Public step 15 explicitly repairs complex-polarization dependence of a time-averaged electric-dipole force, and the exact patch succeeds. Its reward is 1 with no exception. The code contains no pulse time, envelope, component motion or d(Pe)/dt term. The proposed source retains that correct stationary gradient limit; adding the transient canonical-to-kinetic term is not a repair already present in this actual pass. Demonstrated Lorentz-force competence nevertheless creates substantial ease risk.

findings.topic: Pulse r1 and resonator actual passes
findings.verdict: related concepts but not the same solved readout
findings.reason: z8sUiqU predicts whole-body displacement as energy-weighted transit minus length, the complete-body center-of-energy result. That final global constraint does not fix the new inert component at a finite clock. ntqD6wz restores separate internal resonator kinetic and spring energies; the proposed source already includes its transverse oscillator energy and radiation reaction. Neither existing repair alone corrects the new transient force assignment. These comparisons do not prove difficulty.

findings.verdict: genuine force-assignment issue with a known detector filter
findings.reason: The spring and exact oscillator response are shared by source and reference. A causal repair would hold fitted f, optical P(t), clock and mechanical solver fixed and change only the force. The physical distinction is extending a stationary force law to kinetic acceleration during a transient. Merely adding spring modes to a correct force would be extra mathematics; that is not the proposed source error.

specification_items_before_numerics: Explicitly set the complete incident spectrum to a real normalization constant times the compact profile (or give any chosen spectral phase), together with energy normalization and the t=0 clock. The cited r1 README already specifies a real constant, so inheriting it closes the phase; the new sheet specification should say so directly. Spectrum intensity and centroid alone would be insufficient for a non-cycle-averaged finite-clock measurement.
Define the calibration output sign as forward radiation load or the positive magnitude of the opposing support force; the signed holding force itself is negative in the forward convention.

Use a consistent planar per-area or fixed-area normalization for P, f, M and k, and predeclare positive strength, nonresonant calibration, pulse, mechanical-frequency and clock ranges. No finite-body edge-force correction should enter an otherwise ideal planar model.
Fix one bounded feasibility protocol before evaluating gaps. Preserve weak-signal and cancellation cases rather than selecting isolated favorable clocks after inspecting them.
independent_reference_requirements: A time-domain Maxwell characteristic/jump or converged symmetric thin-sheet implementation may obtain both exterior E/B fields and evaluate stress, then integrate Newton equations. It must not use P_dot*e or -P*e_dot as its force input.

Compare against an independently implemented frequency-domain retarded oscillator and mechanical Green-function oracle; refine pulse-tail cutoff, temporal/spectral resolution and any sheet thickness separately.

Check instantaneous optical energy balance, positive U, complete-pulse impulse, stationary calibration equality, zero-strength and mechanical limits, and fixed-clock weak-amplitude scaling. An amplitude-rescaling check of the leading equations is useful but is not an independent proof of finite-amplitude moving-body physics.

Establish ordinary nonzero readout norms and source/oracle separation across the declared domain, then calibration-noise and runtime margins. Reject or defer the proposal if those fail; analytical closure does not justify lowering benchmark gates.

primary_source.title: Bradshaw et al., Electromagnetic Momenta and Forces in Dispersive Dielectric Media
primary_source.access: Opened the primary PDF and read Sec. III Eq. 17-19 and surrounding assumptions. The electric-dipole Lorentz-force decomposition supports the total-derivative distinction. The sheet jumps, stresses, energy, calibration and mechanical kernel are independently derived in this review; the paper's later bulk and narrow-band formulas are not imported.

recommendation: One bounded numerical feasibility calculation is justified after the small specification items above are fixed. This is a coherent same-family closure proposal with a shared identifiable calibration and a distinct transient force error. It is not authorization to package or run a model evaluation, and not a claim of robust separation, a desirable pass rate, or family exhaustion.
